artworks.title: Voyons ... admirez au moins ce Courbet! ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: Two men's upper bodies are shown in the image. The man on the right is leaning forward and reaching out with his hands, wearing a wide-brimmed top hat. His facial expression appears surprised or disbelieving. He has distinctive features including an aquiline nose and a prominent chin, with his hair covered by the hat. He is dressed in a long-sleeved shirt or coat. The man on the left is partially hidden by the other man's arm. His facial expression seems shocked or excited. He wears a rounded hat and has curly hair and a bushy mustache. Both men wear dark-toned jackets and shirts. The background features sketchy depictions of frames and paintings on the wall, suggesting an art gallery or exhibition setting.

artworks.title: Study for "Riverfront No. 1"
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase through a gift of Emily Crane Chadbourne, Charles C. Glover, Jr., and Arthur C. Nash, 1977)
artworks.description: The drawing depicts a figure bending forward, with their back towards the viewer. The figure's body has abstract and disproportionate features, like elongated limbs and a large, exaggerated head. The use of shading and bold lines create depth and contrast. The drawing style suggests an exploration of form and movement in a minimalist and abstract manner.

artworks.title: Une plaisanterie dont ne se lasse ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This is a drawing of swimmers in water. In the foreground, one figure appears to be pushing another's head under the water, both with playful expressions. Another swimmer is shown with only their head visible, trying to stay afloat. Above the water is a structure resembling a stone wall or dock, with several figures looking down at the swimmers. They are sketched in outline in various poses. The artistic style suggests a comedic intent with exaggerated expressions and actions, typical of caricature illustrations.

artworks.title: Mon chagrin c'est de ne pouvoir ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: There are four individuals in the image. The first person on the left is standing, facing the other three. He has a beard, wears a hat, a coat, trousers, and shoes, holding a cane. The second person in the center is smiling broadly, has a prominent nose, and short hair. They are only wearing shorts. One child is on the second person's back, and the other is standing beside them. The scene is set in a simple indoor space with linear patterns on the walls.

artworks.title: Association en commandite our l'exposition de l'humanité a la santé des pratiques
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a scene at a dining table. The image features two skeletal figures sitting across from each other at a table set with a bottle and glasses. The scene takes place under a sign that reads "Au rendez-vous des bons vivants." In the background, there is a depiction of a figure with a scythe. The setting gives off a commentary on mortality and indulgence, highlighted by the phrase above the figures that reads "Association en commandite pour l'exploitation de l'humanité." The drawing employs fine lines and cross-hatching techniques typical of 19th-century satirical illustrations.

artworks.title: Tiens, le moineau a été sepercher
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image shows two men in a wooded area. The man on the left is pointing upward with his left hand, holding something small in his right hand. He is wearing a cap, a long-sleeved shirt, knee-length shorts, and shoes. The man on the right is wearing a cap and holding a firearm in his left hand while leaning on it for support. He is dressed in a long-sleeved coat, knee-length shorts, and shoes. The background features trees with leaf-covered branches.

artworks.title: Allons bon ... c'est encore mon chien ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a hunter and a fallen dog. The drawing depicts the hunter aiming a double-barrel shotgun and observing a dog lying on its back with its legs up in the air. The background consists of a sketchy landscape. The hunter is wearing traditional hunting attire and is seen from behind. The drawing contains a caption in French.

artworks.title: Nude with Cherubim
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1951)
artworks.description: The image features a woman's upper body, with closed eyes and a serene expression. Her hair is elegantly styled and she is partially clothed, with fabric draped across her shoulders and arms. Surrounding her are several cherubic figures with small wings. One cherub rests its head on her shoulder, while others are positioned playfully around her arms. The background is abstract with flowing, textured shading, creating a sense of depth and movement. The artwork appears to be a detailed sketch emphasizing the interaction between the woman and the cherubs.

artworks.title: Venus, Mars, and Cupid
artworks.medium: charcoal with white chalk on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1951)
artworks.description: Three figures are shown, with two of them seated or reclining, partially covered by draped fabric. The first figure is a woman in profile, holding an object in one hand. The second figure is a man seen from the back with short, textured hair, and a child is seated next to him with curly hair. The figures have muscular features and wear minimal clothing. The background includes foliage, distant cliffs, birds in flight, and a columned structure.

artworks.title: Revenge
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: The image is a pencil sketch of a person's upper torso and head, with a stern expression. The person is holding a sword with both hands, leaning slightly forward. The face shows furrowed brows, a broad nose, and tightly pressed lips. The hair is curly or wavy. The clothing is loosely drawn, with a possibly open shirt. The sword's hilt has some decorative elements. The background is blank.

artworks.title: Beached Vessel
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Alice F. Williams, 1958)

artworks.title: Oaks, Wolf Hill, Ulster County
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Kate Bunner, wife of the artist, 1902)
artworks.description: The image shows a pencil sketch of trees from a low perspective. The dense foliage obscures the horizon, creating an immersive view of the natural scene. The detailed pencil strokes capture the branches and leaves with shading. The color palette is monochromatic, using gray tones against light paper. The focus is on the trees, with some depth created by lighter shading in the distance.

artworks.title: Trees, West Virginia
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Kate Bunner, wife of the artist, 1902)
artworks.description: The image shows a pencil drawing of a tall tree with a slender trunk and full, sprawling branches. The tree is detailed with a focus on the texture and density of its foliage, depicted through intricate pencil strokes that convey lightness and movement. The background is light-toned, emphasizing the monochromatic color palette of various shades of gray and natural beige. Minimal details in the backdrop keep the focus on the tree.

artworks.title: Potomac River Below Harper's Ferry
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Kate Bunner, wife of the artist, 1902)
artworks.description: The image is a sketch of a riverside scene. It shows textured rocks on the riverbank, sparse vegetation, and a leaning tree. In the distance, there are hills or low mountains partially covered with trees. The river flows smoothly, reflecting light, with some rapids further away. The sketch is detailed and monochrome, done with pencil strokes.

artworks.title: Hudson; and Claverack Creek
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Kate Bunner, wife of the artist, 1902)
artworks.description: The image shows two landscape sketches positioned vertically on one sheet. The top sketch depicts a tranquil scene with a river flowing horizontally across the image, trees and shrubs along the riverbanks, and a tall tree on the right. The second sketch below shows a creek surrounded by dense vegetation, with trees and branches arching over the water. The sketches are characterized by fine pencil strokes capturing the textures and forms of the natural environment. The colors are primarily in shades of grey, creating a serene and monochromatic visual impact.

artworks.title: Brush; and Hudson Brush Fence
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Kate Bunner, wife of the artist, 1902)
artworks.description: The image shows a pencil drawing of a close-up natural scene. In the upper section, there are detailed branches and leaves entwined together. The artist used controlled strokes to depict the texture of the wood and foliage with attention to light and shadow. The lower part of the drawing shows more branches and undergrowth with delicate brushwork to highlight the details of the leaves and twigs. The color palette is monochromatic with varying shades of grey. The horizon is not visible in the composition focused on interlocking branches and vegetation.

artworks.title: Trees, Hudson
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Kate Bunner, wife of the artist, 1902)
artworks.description: The drawing features a leaning tree at the center dominating the composition. The horizon is not clearly defined, and the land slopes downward towards the left side. Other vegetation and a tree stump are visible beyond the leaning tree. The artist uses precise pencil strokes to depict the foliage and texture of the tree bark. The color palette is grayscale, creating a soft, natural look. The background fades subtly, showing depth and distance, while shadowing and contouring provide clarity to the closest elements. The paper shows spots and discoloration, adding an aged character to the artwork.

artworks.title: Blackberry
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Kate Bunner, wife of the artist, 1902)
artworks.description: The image displays a pencil drawing of a blackberry plant. The stem has thorns and leaves distributed along its length. The drawing is in shades of gray on a light background. The branch extends from the left to the right, with leaves pointing in different directions. An inscription reads "Blackberry Oct 66" at the bottom center.

artworks.title: The Deserted Pigpen; and West Hurley
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Kate Bunner, wife of the artist, 1902)
artworks.description: The drawing consists of two sketches on the same sheet of paper. The upper sketch displays a stone and wooden structure, while the lower sketch depicts a forest with mountains in the background. Fine lines are used to show texture. The lower sketch has a monochromatic color scheme. The paper shows signs of aging.

artworks.title: Seated Male Nude [recto]
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of J. William Middendorf, II, 1977)
artworks.description: The image shows a drawing of a reclined person with one supporting arm and the other resting on a bent knee. The individual's head is slightly turned to the side, providing a profile view of the face. The person has short, straight hair and appears unclothed, with detailed anatomical features. The background is plain and neutral, emphasizing the subject. The artwork is done in pencil or charcoal on paper, with some minor imperfections visible.

artworks.title: Storm at Arbonne
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The painting depicts a rural scene from a slightly elevated perspective. A large stack of hay with a wooden ladder leans against it. A figure tends to a pile of hay at the base. In the background, a village with small cottages and houses surrounded by autumn-colored trees is partially visible. The horizon is low and consists of houses and tree crowns. The sky, rendered in muted shades of gray and beige with soft clouds, occupies more than half of the image. The brushstrokes are smooth and blended, creating a serene, slightly hazy appearance. The color palette is warm and earthy, with browns, soft greens, and grays dominating the scene.

artworks.title: Old Bridge at Weaverton
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Kate Bunner, wife of the artist, 1902)
artworks.description: The image depicts a landscape with a stream flowing in the foreground. Boulders are scattered in the stream. An old stone bridge is visible in the background, partially covered by foliage. The scene has dense foliage blending from the foreground to the background. Tall trees with detailed branches reach up to the top of the image. The drawing style consists of fine pencil lines and shading, creating a serene texture. The color palette is monochromatic, emphasizing pencil shades over vibrant colors.

artworks.title: Elms, Hudson
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Kate Bunner, wife of the artist, 1902)
artworks.description: The image shows a pencil drawing of a natural landscape, focusing on tall trees from a low ground-level perspective. The horizon is low with a faint clearing bordered by more trees in the distance. The pencil technique includes fine lines for texture and depth in the foliage and tree trunks. Shading and cross-hatching depict the canopy density and sunlight filtering through. The color scheme is grayscale with graphite creating a natural impact. The drawing displays energetic scribbling for tree branches and undergrowth, while the background has minimalistic detail, conveying tranquility and space.

artworks.title: Cheat River
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Kate Bunner, wife of the artist, 1902)
artworks.description: The image displays a landscape with a river, hills, structures, and trees. The viewpoint is slightly elevated, showcasing these elements. The background shows a range of hills reaching up to the horizon. On the left side, there are structures and trees along the riverbank. The drawing is detailed using pencil work with textured strokes and monochromatic shades of gray. Rocks near the river's edge frame the scene. The image conveys a sense of natural beauty with a focus on detail and shading.
